judgements.justification: A's chair gave a spotlight that no reviewer argued for (no rating above 7), adding its own 'a novel algorithm design I have never seen'.
Neither recommendation rests on a forecast of impact beyond visual question generation.
No score moved on either committee after the response.

A's reviews took the paper's framing and 'comprehensive evaluation' at face value, asked mostly clarity questions, and Kags (confidence 5) listed mainly typos; none checked the margins or the missing DH-VQG comparisons that B checked.
Only B raised that DH-VQG is missing from the human study and Section 3.4 and that the augmentation gains are marginal, and its chair cited these as grounds for rejection.

Both saw the step beyond DH-VQG and got the same zero-shot table; A called the idea very novel and the rebuttal 'a particularly good job', B called the novelty limited and the results short of comparison.
No reviewer changed a score after discussion.
6a7g's 6 with positive text is one point below its peers and on the accept side; no clear mismatch.
All confidences are 4 or 5; no reviewer said they could not judge the paper.
Neither committee had an outlying reviewer; A's chair paraphrased two typical reviewers.
The verbal assessments differed: A praised novelty, B called it incremental.
A's chair did not cite the reviewers' agreement as grounds for the tier, and B's mean was lower, not similar or higher.
No score rose after the rebuttal.
A's meta-review mentioned the reviewers' significance concerns before saying the rebuttal answered them.
A's nCHe stated that the experiments had appropriate baselines, but DH-VQG is absent from the human study, augmentation and zero-shot results; that error fed A's accept score.
The response told A's pdQY that no ground truth exists for visual hints, conceding the paper's key novelty cannot be tested directly, yet nobody lowered a score and A's chair praised the rebuttal.
tJc4's post-discussion note restated earlier concerns; no new objection arrived after the response period.
The reviews themselves differed (7/6/7/7 vs 5/4/5/5 with different arguments), so the split is not a tier cut-off.
A's most confident reviewer (Kags, 5) voted accept, as the chair did; B's chair followed its unanimous reviewers.
No committee's scores moved after the rebuttal, so the response lifted neither.
No outlying score on either committee.
No outlying reviewer on either committee.
A had no detractor to set aside.
B's chair suggested a vision or NLP venue only as an afterthought; its grounds were novelty and missing comparisons, not audience fit.
Neither meta-review clearly misreported reviewer positions; A's view that the rebuttal settled significance is a judgement, not a misstatement of record.
Reviewers on both committees left the response largely unanswered and none revised, so there is no contrast.
No reviewer said they could not verify the results.
Neither committee was split.
Both committees received the same zero-shot table and novelty statement.
A's pdQY, repeated by A's chair, called double-hint VQG 'new', although the paper credits that setting to Kai et al. [20]; that novelty verdict fed A's score and spotlight.
A's spotlight rests on no rating above 7 and a meta-review that argues only for acceptance, so nothing in A's record supports the higher tier.
B's task-value doubts came from VQG reviewers, not from a neighbouring field's premises.
No reviewer on either committee rated well above the accept level.
B did not reject on the size of promised revisions.

reasoning: Committee A's reviewers accepted the paper's novelty and evaluation at face value, including a wrong 'new problem' claim and a wrong 'appropriate baselines' claim, while B checked the evidence and found DH-VQG missing from key experiments and the gains marginal. The two committees weighed the same step beyond DH-VQG and the same zero-shot table oppositely. A's chair then gave a spotlight that no reviewer argued for. Existing reasons R01, R04, R05, R06, R15, R16, R30 and R31 cover these mechanisms; candidate causes such as 'only one committee checked effect sizes' and 'task significance doubted' fit R05 and R04 on a plain reading, so no reason is added.
